name: fffuel
tagline: 67 free browser generators for SVG backgrounds, patterns, gradients and color tools
description: fffuel is a single-author collection of 67 free, browser-based SVG generators and color utilities, each on its own vowel-tripled subpage (ffflux, gggrain, nnnoise, bbblurry, ssshape and so on). Every tool is a live editor with randomize and parameter controls that outputs copy-pasteable SVG markup, and a few emit CSS or PNG. It is aimed at web designers and front-end developers who need a one-off decorative asset — a mesh gradient, a grain overlay, a wave divider, a blob — without opening Figma or Illustrator.

pricing_detail: Free. No account, no paid tier. A separate desktop color-picker app is offered at /app/.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a landing page needs a distinctive background and you would otherwise ship a flat gradient: ffflux for organic mesh gradients, gggrain for the grain-over-gradient look, nnnoise for a texture overlay you can layer above an existing hero. The output is raw inline SVG, so run it through eeencode and drop the result into a Tailwind arbitrary value (bg-[url('data:image/svg+xml;base64,...')]) rather than shipping a separate file. Watch the payload — turbulence-heavy SVGs from ffflux and gggrain are tens of KB and repaint expensively when scaled, so pin a fixed viewBox and avoid animating them.
why_it_matters: It is the single densest free source of production-ready decorative SVG on the web, and the one bookmark that replaces a dozen single-purpose generator sites. The license is unusually permissive for a free tool: commercial use, no attribution.
evidence: https://fffuel.co (WebFetch, full tool table), https://www.fffuel.co/ (curl, 68 hrefs enumerated), https://www.fffuel.co/about/, https://www.fffuel.co/license/

name: Noun Project Seamless Patterns
tagline: Stock-icon search page: 1,873 pattern-themed glyphs, CC BY free or paid royalty-free
description: This is a search-term page inside Noun Project, the long-running stock icon marketplace, filtered to the term 'seamless pattern' and returning 1,873 contributor-uploaded glyphs. These are single-colour icons that depict or reference patterns — they are not tileable pattern fills. Download is free as black-only PNG or SVG with mandatory CC BY attribution to the artist, or royalty-free without attribution under a NounPro subscription. Useful if you need a pattern-themed pictogram; the wrong tool if you need an actual repeating background.
pricing_detail: Free download with CC BY attribution (black only, no editor). Single icon $4.99. NounPro $3.33/mo billed yearly (unlimited icons). NounPro Plus $9.99/mo billed yearly (icons, icon sets, photos). Paid tiers are royalty-free, worldwide, perpetual, no attribution.
agent_guidance: Do not reach for this to build a background — the results are pictograms of patterns, not tileable fills; use Hero Patterns or fffuel for that. Reach for it only when a project needs a specific, obscure pictogram that Lucide, Phosphor and Heroicons do not cover, and remember the free tier legally requires a visible artist credit in the shipped product, which is a licensing trap in commercial work. There is a public API, so prefer programmatic search over scraping this browse page.
why_it_matters: Noun Project is the deepest icon corpus on the web (nearly 10 million assets), so it is the fallback when a curated open set has no match — but the attribution requirement on the free tier makes it a deliberate, not a default, choice.
notable_for: CC BY free tier needs artist credit

name: Nucleo SVG Patterns
tagline: Free layerable SVG pattern generator with 179 grid, dot, line and tile variants
description: A free single-page generator from Nucleo (the 43,450-icon library) that builds seamless SVG background patterns from a fixed catalogue of 179 pattern variants across 31 families — grids, dot grids, checkerboards, crosshairs, diagonal and dashed lines, circle and square tiles. You can stack several patterns in one canvas, reorder them by drag, set per-layer colour and opacity, set a background colour, and copy the result as clean SVG for CSS, HTML or React. It is aimed at developers building the restrained grid-and-dot backdrops common in modern dashboard and SaaS UI.
pricing_detail: The pattern generator is free. The parent Nucleo icon library is paid: All Icons bundle $299/yr; Core Icons $99; UI Icons $99; Sharp Icons $69; Pixel Icons $69; Micro Bold Icons $69 — one-time payment with lifetime updates.
agent_guidance: This is the right generator when you want the quiet grid or dot-grid backdrop behind a dashboard or hero — its output is geometric and small, unlike the turbulence-heavy SVGs from fffuel, so it inlines cheaply as a data URI. Use the layering feature to combine a coarse grid with a fine dot grid in one asset instead of stacking two background layers in CSS. Note the licence forbids redistribution and explicitly forbids using the patterns to build a competing generator, so do not vendor the catalogue into your own registry — generate per project and copy the output.
why_it_matters: It hits the exact aesthetic that shadcn-era dashboards want (subtle grids, dotted planes) with cleaner, lighter markup than the blob-and-gradient generators, and it costs nothing despite sitting inside a paid product.
notable_for: free tool inside a paid icon product
evidence: https://nucleoapp.com/svg-patterns (WebFetch), https://nucleoapp.com/svg-patterns/ (curl, 179 pattern ids counted in source), https://nucleoapp.com/pricing (WebFetch)

name: MagicPattern
tagline: 45 background, gradient, halftone and dither generators behind a $10-20/mo plan
description: MagicPattern is a hosted toolbox of 45 graphic generators covering seamless and geometric patterns, mesh and blurry gradients, shader backgrounds, halftone and CMYK dot effects, dithering, god rays, fractal glass, blobs, confetti and CSS-only pattern backgrounds, plus a set of SVG/Base64 conversion utilities. Exports run to PNG, JPG, SVG, CSS, WebP and GIF, and a social-media editor and wallpaper library sit alongside the generators. A handful of generators are free to use; the full suite, unlimited exports, saved graphics and commercial/resale rights sit behind a subscription.

pricing_detail: Basic $10/mo or $120/yr. Pro $20/mo or $240/yr. One-time passes: 3 months Basic $49, 6 months Basic $79 (creditable toward an annual plan). Enterprise pricing on request for API/widget use. Both paid tiers grant commercial use and resale of exported graphics; a few generators (blobs, waves, palette) are free.
agent_guidance: Use MagicPattern when the effect is genuinely hard to hand-roll — halftone, CMYK dots, dithering, fractal glass, shader gradients — and skip it for plain patterns and blobs, which fffuel and Nucleo do free. It is a raster-first tool for the interesting effects: expect PNG/WebP, not inline SVG, so budget for an image request and a width/height rather than a data URI. The paywall means you cannot script it; hand the user the tool link and have them export, or fall back to the free CSS-pattern pages under /tools/css-backgrounds which are copyable without an account.
why_it_matters: It is the broadest single-vendor generator suite, and the only mainstream one that covers print-style raster effects (halftone, dither, CMYK) rather than only web gradients — but the subscription puts it out of reach for casual and automated use.
notable_for: halftone, dither and CMYK print effects

name: SVG Backgrounds
tagline: 200+ browser-customizable SVG website backgrounds, 48 free, rest on a $120/yr plan
description: SVG Backgrounds (Visiwig LLC, by Matt Visiwig) is a subscription library of over 200 SVG website backgrounds that you recolour to your brand in the browser and paste straight into a site — some animate, shrink, spin or shift. Roughly 48 of them are free; the rest, plus icons, freebies and a set of free SVG generators, sit behind a $120/yr subscription with an extended-license upgrade. The subscription model is deliberate: the value is the in-browser customiser, not a zip of files.
pricing_detail: $120/yr subscription. ~48 backgrounds free. Extended License sold separately. Graphics already placed in projects stay usable after the subscription lapses, but you cannot add new ones.
agent_guidance: Treat this as a human-only destination: the site sits behind a Cloudflare interstitial and returns 403 to every automated fetch, so you cannot read the catalogue, scrape a background, or verify a licence programmatically — link the user to it and let them export. For agent-driven work pick Hero Patterns (CC BY, 87 patterns, readable source) or fffuel (free, unrestricted) instead. Only recommend it when the user specifically wants the animated or brand-recoloured backgrounds it is known for and is willing to pay.
why_it_matters: One of the older curated background libraries with a genuinely useful in-browser recolour flow, but the paywall plus a hard bot block make it a poor fit for an index that AI agents query.
evidence: https://www.svgbackgrounds.com/ (WebFetch 403, curl 403 Cloudflare 'Just a moment' challenge), https://www.svgbackgrounds.com/backgrounds/ (WebFetch 403), https://www.svgbackgrounds.com/set/free-svg-backgrounds-and-patterns/ (WebFetch 403). Counts, pricing and authorship come from WebSearch result snippets of the site's own /license/, /subscribe/ and /set/ pages, NOT from on-page reading.

name: Hero Patterns
tagline: 87 free CC BY repeatable SVG patterns, copied out as a CSS data-URI background
description: Hero Patterns is Steve Schoger's collection of 87 hand-drawn, tileable SVG background patterns — Topography, Circuit Board, Jigsaw, Hexagons, Endless Clouds, Bank Note and so on. Pick a pattern, set the foreground colour, opacity and background colour, then copy the generated CSS (a background-image data URI) or download the unstyled SVG. It is free under CC BY 4.0 and has been the default source of subtle web background texture since 2016.
agent_guidance: This is the fastest path to a textured section background: the site hands you a finished `background-image: url("data:image/svg+xml,...")` string, so paste it into a Tailwind arbitrary value or a CSS custom property and you are done — no asset pipeline, no extra request. Keep opacity around 0.05-0.1 and set the fill to a token colour so the pattern survives a dark-mode swap, since the data URI bakes the colour in and will not respond to CSS variables. Reach for Nucleo SVG Patterns instead when you need a plain grid or dot grid; Hero Patterns' catalogue is illustrative and reads as decorative, and its 2016-era motifs (Skulls, Charlie Brown, Piano Man) will date a page fast.
why_it_matters: The canonical free SVG pattern set — CC BY, still online after a decade, and the only one whose output is already a paste-ready CSS declaration, which is exactly the shape an agent wants.
evidence: https://heropatterns.com (WebFetch), https://heropatterns.com/js/app.js (curl, 87 pattern names extracted), https://github.com/sschoger/hero-patterns (WebFetch), https://api.github.com/repos/sschoger/hero-patterns (stars 59, pushed_at 2021-11-12, no license, not archived)
